key_insight: Matrix-product-state (MPS) encoding makes non-local pseudopotentials practical in first-quantized quantum simulation by sharply lowering Trotter-step circuit depth.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more hardware-feasible route to quantum chemistry and strong-field simulation, especially where pseudopotentials reduce electron count but introduce difficult non-local operators.
method: Encode the wave function in MPS form instead of direct unitary decomposition
Implement non-local pseudopotentials efficiently through the MPS structure
Combine with first-quantized Trotterization to reduce depth to O(deg(V_loc) n^deg(V_loc) + 8Lnn_atomχ^2 + 2n^2)
evidence_signal: The authors tested the approach on ionization of a one-dimensional hydrogen atom driven by an ultrashort laser pulse and reported significantly lower circuit depth than direct unitary decomposition.
watch_item: The depth advantage depends on MPS bond dimension χ and pseudopotential structure, so performance may degrade for more entangled or higher-dimensional systems.
paper_title: First-quantized quantum simulation with non-local potentials by matrix-product-state encoding
